questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of deleting branches?
options: Deleting a merged local branch is a cleanup step after confirming the work is integrated. Prefer the safe `-d` form; force-deleting an unmerged branch can remove the only convenient reference to important work.
Git automatically backs up every file, including ignored and untracked files, to a remote.
The operation grants every contributor write access to the hosted repository.
questions.answer_key: Deleting a merged local branch is a cleanup step after confirming the work is integrated. Prefer the safe `-d` form; force-deleting an unmerged branch can remove the only convenient reference to important work.
questions.explanation: Deleting a merged local branch is a cleanup step after confirming the work is integrated. Prefer the safe `-d` form; force-deleting an unmerged branch can remove the only convenient reference to important work.

questions.prompt: Which command is the most direct starting point for this lesson’s example?
questions.explanation: Use `git branch -d feature/example` as the first inspection/action in the example, and then verify the result with the companion checks in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest general practice when working with deleting branches?
options: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
Run the most destructive option first; the reflog guarantees every file can always be recovered.
Assume the local command also changed the remote and satisfied all hosting-platform policies.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
questions.explanation: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
